What are your favorite recent (released in 2010 or later) puzzle games?

Hey, profanion! Not many puzzlers have interested me nowadays (man, the only genre I had it for a while...), but I definitely picked up some great ones there. Most of these are optimization puzzle games that actually have replay value; there are more of those that I like, so I'll highlight the ones that are NOT programming based.

Manufactoria - 2010. One of the earliest puzzle programming games so it's very rough around the edges -- I'd even say around the center now --, but it's enjoyable. About robots, but gameplay-wise about recoloring tapes.
English Country Tune - 2011. Not a programming game. Very abstract, control various objects like a beam or a square in a 3D world to move around other objects to their respective spots. Yes they're balls.
SpaceChem - 2011. Good classic. I however also did not enjoy the ultimate 'boss' puzzles for each chapter. However, it's relatively flexible. Control 'waldos' that can pick up, drop, bond, etc. atoms to make molecules.
LogicBox Flash - 2012. Best function-representation of programming I can think of that doesn't actually say it.
Sokobond - 2014. Not programming based. Takes that molecule idea and instead mixes it with Sokoban (block pushing game).
Great Permutator - 2014. 2D plane puzzler where you use conveyors and machines to change box order and color.
Snakebird - 2015. Not programming based. Turns Snake from a top down view into a platformer perspective with gravity, and makes it turn based, basically.
Infinifactory - 2015. "SpaceChem in 3D". Uses more physical options than SpaceChem and generally more flexible/larger 'worlds'. Unfortunately, it's not open world.
LogicBox HTML5 - 2016 (ehh on the date, could be 2018 at this point) Greatly expanded version of LB on Flash. Highly recommended since it actually fixes many of the problems many of the other games have issues with.

Look guys, I didn't know they would all be so evenly spaced out :P Note that I can only speak of games I have played. There are a few puzzlers I have my eye on, but I have no confidence in their quality.

The last puzzle game I really enjoyed was Antichamber. I had to look at the wiki at some parts though, sometimes it was really unclear what to do next. Overall it was a good, relaxing mindbender with some unique game mechanics.
I really liked Catherine. I know its not everyone's cup of tea, but I really had a great time with that game.
